name: NGC 1832, SN 2009kr field (Hubble)
blurb: NGC 1832, a spiral galaxy that hosted the Type II supernova SN 2009kr, seen by Hubble.
label: sn2009kr-hubble
story: In this spiral galaxy a supernova, SN 2009kr, burst from a star that earlier Hubble images suggest was a yellow supergiant. Hubble came back after the blast faded to see whether that star was gone.

claims.text: SN 2009kr was found in the spiral galaxy NGC 1832
SN 2009kr is a type II supernova
A source in HST pre-explosion images, if a single star, would be a yellow supergiant
The program images faded core-collapse supernova sites to confirm the progenitors are gone; SN 2009kr is a target
